text: A context manager guarantees that cleanup happens, no matter how your code exits.
Any class with two special methods can be one — enter and exit.
Enter runs when the with block starts, and whatever it returns is what you bind with as.
Here it prints starting and hands back the object itself.
Exit runs when the block finishes, and star exc catches any exception details Python passes in.
It prints done, then returns False, meaning don't suppress errors — let them propagate.
If exit returned True instead, it would swallow the exception entirely, which is rarely what you want.
Now the with statement itself. Timer parentheses creates the object and enters it.
This is exactly how open works when you read a file with a with statement.
Inside the block we do the actual work.
Starting, then working, then done — and that done is guaranteed even if the body raises.
